description:
## Why This Exists

post/did_verify.rs::strip_did_sig_header() splits on b'
' to process lines, then rejoins with b'
'.as_slice(). If the original article used CRLF line endings, all  characters are preserved in each line segment (since split on 
 keeps the ). But the rejoined output correctly has 
 on each line EXCEPT the last — the trailing 
 after the last line is added by join, not from the original.

If the original article ends with 
 (as all RFC 5536 NNTP articles should), the rejoined article ends with 

 (extra 
 from join). This corrupts the byte content and causes DID signature verification to fail on well-formed CRLF articles.

The test strip_did_sig_header_preserves_non_utf8_bytes uses CRLF input and CRLF expected output — does that test pass? If it does, the join does NOT add an extra 
. Verify.

## Acceptance Criteria

Add a test that strips the DID-Sig header from a CRLF article and byte-compares the result against the expected CRLF output. If the test fails, fix the rejoining logic.
